# FDG5112

> DO be aware that mutable arguments might have changed after they were validated.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.8.2 Validating Arguments.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Not checked: whether an argument can change after it is validated depends on its type and on other threads, and whether a member is security-sensitive is a design fact.

## From the book

If the member is security-sensitive, you are encouraged to make a copy and then validate and process the argument.

> **Rico Mariani:** This is one of the many places where you can cash in on the fact that CLR strings are immutable; there is no need to copy them in security-sensitive operations.
